Agent.text: The check passes. Now I'll update the two open questions to record what I did in their place.

I built **OpenViz**, a free, open-source (MIT licence) desktop app for exploring data. You open a spreadsheet saved as CSV, or start with the built-in sample shop data. You build charts by dragging fields onto Columns, Rows, Color, Size, Label and Filters, and it makes bar, line, area, scatter, pie, heat map and table charts, with sorting, undo, formula fields, several sheets and a dashboard. You can save your work and reopen it, and export a sheet's numbers or a picture of the window. It builds, the automatic checks I added pass, and Craft Anything's check says it would pass.

I never saw the original, because there was no picture of it to work from. So the look follows how this kind of app is usually laid out, under its own name and with no copied logos or branding.

It only opens CSV files, not Excel files or the original program's own saved files. Maps, live database connections and online sharing are left for later rounds.

A good next step is to send me a screenshot of the original, or tell me which of those missing features you'd use most. Excel files and maps are the most common requests.
